findings.title: The opening as a judicial truth-test
findings.claim: The focus opening carries both the public event the challengers demand and the judgment that settles their dispute: the prior declaration that the Lord separates disputing parties activates its adjudicative sense, while the challenge about truth makes its arrival a test whose result comes too late to make their prior denial beneficial.
findings.mechanism: The repeated opening in 32:28 is framed as proof of truth; 32:25 supplies an explicit scene of the Lord separating parties over what they disputed. When 32:29 names the day of the opening and pairs established denial with faith that no longer benefits, the opening can be heard as access, ruling, victory, and disclosure together. The opening meets the denial-as-covering image, while the challenged truth meets faith as assent; the no-benefit clause fixes the consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the answer to the demand for a date is also a cutoff: the opening may verify the warning as victory and adjudication, but belief offered at that point cannot change the outcome.
findings.containment: The ordinary day-of-opening reading and the explicit no-benefit/no-respite force remain intact. Victory and adjudication coexist; the packet does not choose one exclusive referent. The challenge may be mockery rather than a sincere plan to believe after proof, and the HFT trace does not establish individual motives.

epistemic.reason: The channel nominations have trusted status and the focus morphology is supplied. The additional 32:25 and 32:28 HFT roles have exact Arabic anchors but legacy-unbound context segmentation, so they are retained as attributed evidence.

findings.title: No further time, with a faint echo of regard
findings.claim: The final passive verb primarily denies further waiting or respite, while its perception branch can add a faint echo of no further regard: the prior verse asks whether they see, and the following verse turns the messenger away.
findings.mechanism: The focus root supplies both a registered waiting/respite branch and a registered directed-attention branch. The failure-to-see question in 32:27 and the attributed turn-away in 32:30 independently touch the attention branch and return through the focus verb, while its passive form and focus context keep granted respite as the primary reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The no-respite clause gains a small relational shade: after signs have gone unseen, consideration itself can feel withdrawn along with time.
findings.containment: The eye/regard reading remains an exploratory echo and never replaces the focus's denial of respite. The prior seeing verb and focus nẓr are different supplied roots; their contact is contextual, not lexical identity. The following turn-away role is HFT-attributed.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace provides exact Arabic anchors and focus return, but its context root/index mapping is legacy-unbound and the passive focus morphology strongly favors the respite reading.

findings.title: Denial beside provision
findings.claim: The focus denial verb can carry an exploratory ingratitude shade because 32:27 places water, crops, and food beside a question about whether the sign is seen; the focus group may therefore be heard against provision as well as religious denial.
findings.mechanism: The focus word maps to the accepted branch for denying a blessing or failing to show gratitude. The immediate context supplies water reaching barren land and food emerging from it; that concrete provision meets the branch through the focus denial verb, without a gratitude term in the focus itself.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see a local contrast between provision made visible and the focus's group defined by denial.
findings.containment: This does not translate kafarū as ungrateful, assert that the group rejected this specific water, or displace the focus's religious-denial reading. The absent gratitude term and unproven identity link keep this an exploratory contextual inference.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch is registered and the preceding context text is supplied, but the context-root trace is legacy-unbound and no explicit gratitude marker or direct subject link is present.
